question: Why does the rule "Preserve both behavioral and structural value" matter in a code review?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Preserve both behavioral and structural value
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 23: The Two Values of Software, PR review rules
Preserve both behavioral and structural value

relevant_concepts: Preserve both behavioral and structural value
Software delivers behavior, but its structure determines how cheaply and safely future behavior can be changed. A system that works today but resists change has lost a core part of its value.

question: What fix does the guidance recommend for "Keep policy separate from detail"?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Keep policy separate from detail
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 23: The Two Values of Software, PR review rules
Keep policy separate from detail

relevant_concepts: Isolate details behind adapters and ports so policy can execute without knowing the delivery or storage mechanism.

question: What review guidance applies to "Keep interfaces agnostic about delivery mechanisms"?

expected_rule_sections.heading: Keep interfaces agnostic about delivery mechanisms
heading_path: Clean Code, Chapter 23: The Two Values of Software, PR review rules
Keep interfaces agnostic about delivery mechanisms

relevant_concepts: Keep interfaces agnostic about delivery mechanisms
Delivery mechanisms change independently of business rules. Keeping policy agnostic allows the same behavior to be exposed through different interfaces and makes experiments cheaper.
